helper_distribution.runtime_note: publish output includes the .NET runtime; no separately installed .NET runtime is required

candidates.symbol_resolution: full SemanticModel/Symbol APIs for resolved compilations
candidates.incomplete_source_recovery: compiler syntax trees and diagnostics remain available for many invalid/incomplete inputs
candidates.packaging: self-contained helper folder bundled under backends/csharp

candidates.symbol_resolution: syntax-only; cannot resolve semantic cast/overload ambiguities by itself
candidates.overload_resolution: none without a separate semantic layer

candidates.syntax_fidelity: insufficient for semantic Common IR analysis

helper_semantic_strategy.project_sources: collect project C# sources and create Roslyn syntax trees/compilations
helper_semantic_strategy.framework_references: derive runtime framework metadata references inside the self-contained helper
helper_semantic_strategy.project_references: resolve source/project references through Tomiya project discovery; do not require MSBuildWorkspace initially
helper_semantic_strategy.unity_references: use project-resolvable Unity assemblies when available; unresolved external symbols must remain explicitly unresolved
helper_semantic_strategy.common_ir_boundary: only normalized Common IR/wire DTOs cross into the Python host

known_limits: Full semantic resolution depends on having enough project source and metadata references.
Unity/editor-specific assemblies may be unresolved when the project does not expose usable references.
MSBuildWorkspace is not required in the initial helper design to avoid an SDK/MSBuild runtime dependency.
tree-sitter-c-sharp remains a possible fallback for malformed editor buffers if Roslyn recovery proves insufficient for a product use case.

integration.windows_delivery: self-contained win-x64 folder copied into PyInstaller onedir
